reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any complete real inner-product space, s any subset of E, f : E → ℝ any real-valued function, m any real number, and grad : E → E any supplied vector field. Assume s is convex and f is m-strongly convex on s in the following precise sense: for every u,v ∈ s and every a,b ≥ 0 with a+b=1, f(a u+b v) ≤ a f(u)+b f(v)−a b (m/2) ‖u−v‖². Assume also that for every z ∈ s, f has an ambient Fréchet derivative at z represented by grad(z) under the real inner product. Then for all x,y ∈ s, m‖y−x‖² ≤ ⟨grad(y)−grad(x),y−x⟩. This is a one-way implication from strong convexity plus ambient differentiability to the displayed gradient difference lower bound. When m>0 this gives strong monotonicity on s with constant m, and when m=0 ordinary monotonicity; for negative m the displayed inequality must not be read as ordinary monotonicity. It asserts no converse, minimizer existence, uniqueness, or Lipschitz bound for grad. There is no requirement that m be positive, s be open, closed, bounded, or nonempty, or E be finite-dimensional. The gradient condition holds at every point of s and is ambient, including at boundary points; it is not just differentiability relative to s. No continuity assumption on grad is imposed. The conclusion concerns only pairs in s.
objects: E; subset s; function f : E → ℝ; real parameter m; vector field grad : E → E; points x,y.
domains: E is a complete real inner-product space; s ⊆ E; m ∈ ℝ without a sign restriction.
quantifiers: Universally quantified E, s, f, m, grad; ambient gradient hypothesis for every z ∈ s; conclusion for every x,y ∈ s. Strong convexity quantifies over every u,v ∈ s and all nonnegative real a,b with a+b=1.
assumptions: StrongConvexOn s m f, including convexity of s and the weighted inequality with subtractive coefficient a b m/2; ambient HasGradientAt f (grad z) z at every z ∈ s.
scopes: All assumptions on strong convexity and conclusions are scoped to s; f and grad are defined on E and derivatives are ambient. No converse or source equivalence is claimed.
constant_dependencies: The coefficient of the squared norm is exactly m, with m the arbitrary real parameter in StrongConvexOn; no additional constants.
